selected_complete_units.body:
Let X be a compact Kähler manifold of dimension n. Let α be a big cohomology
                                           class with a smooth representative θ. Let PSH(X, θ) be the space of θ-psh functions
                                           on X. The mixed Monge–Ampère operator is defined in [BT82] for bounded poten-
                                           tials and in [BEGZ10] for general potentials. The product constructed in [BEGZ10]
                                           is called the non-pluripolar product.
                                              It is nature and important to know if one can perform integration by parts for the
                                           non-pluripolar product. For potentials with small unbounded loci in PSH(X, θ), one
                                           can always reduce the problem to the classical Bedford–Taylor theory with certain
                                           tricks and the integration by parts formula is proved in [BEGZ10] Theorem 1.14
                                           for these potentials.
                                              The general case is not yet proved in literature. We fill the gap in this paper.

selected_complete_units.label: Definitions and full monotonicity statement
selected_complete_units.body:
Monotonicity of nonpluripolar products and relative finite energy. Unless otherwise specified, we fix
a background Kähler structure (X, ω) for the remainder of the paper.
   We say that a potential u ∈ L 1 (X, ωn ) is θ -plurisubharmonic (θ -psh) if locally u is the difference of
a plurisubharmonic and a smooth function, and θu := θ + i∂ ∂u       ¯ ≥ 0 in the sense of currents. The set of
θ -psh potentials is denoted by PSH(X, θ ). We say that {θ } is pseudoeffective if PSH(X, θ ) is nonempty.
Along these lines, {θ } is big if PSH(X, θ − εω) is nonempty for some ε > 0.
   If u and v are two θ-psh functions on X, then u is said to be less singular than v if v ≤ u + C for some
C ∈ R. We say that u has the same singularities as v if u is less singular than v, and v is less singular
than u. This defines an equivalence relation on PSH(X, θ ) whose equivalence classes are the singularity
types [u], u ∈ PSH(X, θ).
                                                                       p
   Given closed positive (1, 1)-currents T1 := θu11 , . . . , T p := θu p , where the θ j are closed smooth real
(1, 1)-forms, generalizing the construction of [Bedford and Taylor 1987] in the local setting, it was shown
in [Boucksom et al. 2010] that one can define the nonpluripolar product of these currents:

                                      θu11 ∧ · · · ∧ θupp := hT1 ∧ · · · ∧ T p i.

The resulting positive ( p, p)-current does not charge pluripolar sets and it is closed. For a θ -psh function u,
the nonpluripolar complex Monge–Ampère measure of u is simply θun := θu ∧ · · · ∧ θu .
   It was recently proved by Witt Nyström [2017, Theorem 1.2] that the complex Monge–Ampère mass
of θ -psh potentials decreases as the singularity type increases. Our main result about monotonicity of
nonpluripolar products generalizes this result to the case of different cohomology classes {θ j }, fully
proving what was conjectured by Boucksom, Eyssidieux, Guedj and Zeriahi (see the comments after
[Boucksom et al. 2010, Theorem 1.16] in which they prove that the result holds for potentials with small
unbounded locus):

Theorem 1.1. Let θ j, j ∈ {1, . . . , n}, be smooth closed real (1, 1)-forms on X. Let u j , v j ∈ PSH(X, θ j )
such that u j is less singular than v j for all j ∈ {1, . . . , n}. Then
                                    Z                          Z

classes are pseudoeffective. Let u j , v j ∈ PSH(X, θ j ) be such that u j has the same singularity type as v j ,
j ∈ {1, . . . , n}. Then

                                          1             n

                                            X                         X

   The proof of this result uses the arguments in [Boucksom et al. 2010, Corollary 2.15].

Proof. First we note that we can assume that the classes {θ j } are in fact big. Indeed, if this is not the
case we can just replace each θ j with θ j + εω, and using the multilinearity of the nonpluripolar product
[Boucksom et al. 2010, Proposition 1.4] we can let ε → 0 at the end of our argument to conclude the
statement for pseudoeffective classes.
   For each t ∈ 1 = {t = (t1 , . . . , tn ) ∈ Rn | t j > 0} consider u t := j t j u j , vt := j t j v j and θ t := j t j θ j.

Theorem 1.2] that X (θutt )n = X (θvtt )n for all t ∈ 1. On the other hand, using multilinearity of the

                                                                                                             R

t → X (θvtt )n are homogeneous polynomials of degree n. Our last identity forces all the coefficients of

application_limits: Xia mixed integration by parts is printed for big classes. A pseudoeffective extension requires a fresh proved add-large-Kahler-form and polynomial-coefficient argument.
DDNL Proposition2.1 and Theorem2.4 explicitly include pseudoeffective classes; Theorem2.3 is printed for big classes.
Equal singularity type means bounded differences of potentials, not equality of multiplier ideals or I-equivalence.
Xia signed dd-c products are differences of nonpluripolar products, not an assumed distributional wedge with arbitrary singular currents.
DDNL uses i-del-delbar; a consistent convention conversion is required for later applications.
The first positive mixed mass of an actual prescribed current is not automatically the numerical dimension of its class.
New energy, path-independence and lower-dimensional-carrier constructions remain unverified.
